propositions: Plan review must execute selected discovery work through the S2 shared typed kernel while preserving current topology, facet packing, fallback ladder, centrality budget, bounded concurrency, and cache warming.

Failed local units cannot serialize as clean checkpoints; earlier successes survive, independent work continues, dependents skip, and final verdict follows the approved BLOCK/INDETERMINATE/PASS policy.

The new checkpoint key must change when any material, code/ref, policy, prompt, contract, model/mode, topology, context, dependency, or namespace input changes; corrupt and legacy entries produce zero reuse.
Only content-identical success/resume envelopes seed checkpoint reuse; failed, cancelled, skipped, and budget-shed units remain missing and callable on later runs.
The reducer-ignored review journal stores the safe versioned trace while review-plan outputs retain only their established end-result contract fields.
